title: Arcadia Bancorp - outbound play & notes
content:
Quick context:
- Arcadia Bancorp: regional bank (~600 branches across midwest). Heavy legacy stack but active cloud migration program (Azure).
- Pain areas surfaced in public filings / local press: rising false positives in AML alerts -> operations overload; customer service complaints about slow digital support and high handoffs.
- Reg-constraints: likely need strong controls (KMS/HSM, VPC), potential requirement for on-prem vault for some datasets.

Hypothesis / value prop to test:
- Replace current rules-heavy AML triage assistant with a hybrid approach: lightweight on-prem model for PII-sensitive steps + Redwood-hosted or Dedicated tiers for computation-heavy reranking and embeddings (or vice versa depending on compliance ask).
- Win = 40% fewer false positives passed to manual review and 30% faster first-response time for customer chat (fewer handoffs).

Signals from their public job postings / tech stack that matter:
- 2x Cloud Platform Eng roles mentioning Azure AKS and Terraform -> they are comfortable with infra-as-code and k8s deployments.
- Several postings for "Fraud Analytics" + Listing of SAS/SQL lineage tools -> likely vectorizable datasets from existing pipeline.
- Security/compliance job listing mentions FIPS-validated crypto -> they take key management seriously.

Primary contacts to target (research notes):
- Head of Digital Experience: Priya Raman (LinkedIn signal: worked at regional bank transformation program 2022-24). Good champion for chat improvements.
- Director Fraud Ops: Marcus Bell — cares about false positive headcount and MTTR.
- Cloud Platform Lead: Ethan Ruiz — gate for private deployment and networking.
- Legal / Compliance: Sarah Nguyen — will own KYC/AML data residency questions.

Quick outreach sequence (play):
1) Short email to Priya (value-first) — try to get intro to Marcus.
2) Follow-up with a one-pager and optional short demo showing 2-minute AML triage flow.
3) If receptive, offer 3-week constrained POC: one AML ruleset + chat channel in parallel.

Draft cold email (short, conversational) -> SUBJECT and BODY as separate lines to make it skimmable:
- SUBJECT: 2-week pilot to cut AML false positives at Arcadia?

- BODY: Hi Priya —
  Quick note: we recently ran a short pilot with a midwest regional bank and helped them cut manual AML triage workload by ~35% using a lightweight inference layer + targeted rules.
  We’re Redwood Inference — focused on putting predictable, production-grade LLM inference in regulated environments (private VPC or dedicated pools).
  I think there’s a low-effort way to validate whether we can reduce your AML backlog by trialing 1 rulebook + 2 weeks of live inference on a small slice of traffic.
  Want to jump on 20 minutes next week to see a short recording + proposed scope?
  - Isabel

Call / discovery script snippets (fast notes):
- 1st 5min: confirm org context (what's current false positive rate, current tooling, SLA for triage).
- Next 10min: show quick demo (synthetic but representative): ingest alert -> embedding + rerank -> show human-in-loop triage UI.
- 5min: talk operations (who owns infra, SLAs, what data can be copied to cloud vs stays on-prem).

Objections & quick rebuttals (scratchy):
- "We can’t send PII to external vendors." -> Redwood Private or on-prem option + KMS/HSM integrations. Emphasize zero-knowledge configuration patterns and audit logs in Console.
- "We already have an ML team." -> Redwood reduces infra and ops lift (runtime, autoscaling, batching) and offers rollouts/guardrails so models are safe in production; we can integrate with their model registry or run our runtime on their VPC.
- "Cost concerns" -> show predictable pricing: reserved Dedicated capacity for steady inference + Optimize recommendations to reduce tokens and suggest quantized model variants. Offer initial discounted pilot.

Back-of-envelope pricing note (very rough for convo):
- Pilot scope: 2 weeks, 1000 alerts/day sample stream (~200k tokens/day during analysis + reranking).
- If run on Dedicated small pool: baseline commit $X/month (we’d propose a pilot credit to avoid heavy upfront). Metric to tie to: cost per triaged alert vs FTE hourly cost.

Pilot proposal (3-week minimal POC):
- Week 0: onboarding + infra prep (networking, KMS, sample data snapshot) -> connect to their dev environment; set up Redwood Private or Dedicated dev pool.
- Week 1: ingest sample alerts, build embedding index, run offline evaluation against labeled historical alerts.
- Week 2: shadow mode on live stream (no human-facing changes) -> measure false positive reduction and latency.
- Week 3: short controlled rollout on one queue + review + handoff plan.
- Acceptance metric: >=20% reduction in alerts escalated to analysts or clear path with action items to reach 30%+.

Metrics to gather during POC:
- baseline FP rate, post-inference FP rate, time-to-resolution (median), analyst hours saved per 1k alerts, system latency P50/P95.
- cost per alert vs current manual cost (analyst fully loaded)

Operational notes (tech asks we will need answers to quickly):
- Can they expose a sandbox event stream or S3 bucket with masked alerts?
- Network: do they allow private peering to our Dedicated region or prefer an on-prem appliance?
- KMS specifics: vendor (Azure Key Vault / HashiCorp HSM / SafeNet) and any FIPS constraints.
- Data retention/legal: how long can we store logs, who can we share prototype artifacts with?

Scripted Slack/DM for intro (to send to Priya if warm):
- "Hi Priya — quick ask: would you be open to a 20-min intro to see a 3-week POC plan for reducing AML false positives? I suspect there’s a quick win without touching core systems; happy to work with Ethan on infra details. — Isabel"

Notes / remind-to-self:
- Ask Darius to draft the one-pager + simple sequence diagram of data flow (redwood private <> bank network).
- Check with infra (Lena) about typical latency numbers on Private vs Dedicated for 512-token rerank path. Need P95 < 300ms if they want near-real-time triage.
- Pull any benchmarks we have for AML-ish workloads (reranking recall/precision gains).

Open questions to resolve before first meeting:
- Can we get a sanitized sample dataset quickly? (this determines offline eval speed)
- Will Legal require an MOU / DSAs pre-demo? Probably yes for anything with live data.
- Who is easiest internal sponsor: Priya (digital) vs Marcus (fraud ops) — prioritize whoever cares most about immediate headcount relief.

Next steps (today / immediate):
- Send initial email to Priya (aim calendar next week).
- Darius: one-pager + network diagram (2 business days).
- Lena: confirm Private latency numbers and pilot credit ask.

Random scratches/ideas to test during POC:
- A/B compare: current rule-only triage vs rule + embedding rerank -> show lift metrics live in Redwood Console.
- Low-friction UX: a "confidence" flag added to their analyst queue so low-confidence hits are deprioritized, speeding up humans.
- Post-pilot: propose dedicated capacity + throttled canary rollout for service-level guarantees.

End of notes.

-- IM
